blind.note: Steps younger than 20000 yr (rescaled) are dropped unless the file's [deep.blind] cites a source dating a decline there, which keeps them (grade D). `against`: dropped steps whose mean level is beyond 1.5x from the youngest resolved step, which the flat span to the next level runs against: said on the card, not drawn.

deep_join.note: How each genomic deep past meets its anchor (ToLaD#143, replacing #77/#80/#71): the genome gives the shape, the anchor the number. The whole genomic curve is scaled by one factor so its young end (pre-modern) meets the higher of the first cited count (a history file's baseline or first point, any year) and the modelled natural level: the count when it is the higher (`next` cited), else the natural level in 1500 CE, from which the range-loss trend runs down to the count (`next` natural); with no cited count, the modelled level (the natural level in 1500 CE, the natural baseline, today's modelled count; `next` modelled). It is held flat to it. ratio = genomic level at its young end / anchor, before scaling; flagged when beyond 10x either way; factor = 1 / ratio, except on a flagged join whose young end is below the median of its resolved steps (ToLaD#172, `meet` median): that median meets the anchor instead (factor = anchor / res_median_raw) and the young steps it puts below the anchor are held at it (`held`), so the deep past peaks at most res_max_raw / res_median_raw above the anchor; not where [deep.blind] cites the young end's decline (the lion). Per species: history.species[<sp>].deep.join (its `note` is the card's sentence).

mutation_rate.note: Per-lineage mutation rate per site per year (ToLaD#74, #75): log10 mu_y = a + b log10 G + offset[order], G = the pipeline's generation length (2L, years). Fit over the modelled per-year rates of the pedigree mammals of the source; an order gets an offset (the mean residual of its species) from 2 species. lo / hi = mu x/ 10^band_dex (the 95% prediction band).
